author: Michael Mastelero
text:
CGMs are not live. They are usually 20 minutes behind. You cannot compare their readings to a blood glucose monitor as they measure from 2 different sources — CGMs measure from interstitial fluids (hence the delay), BGMs measure from the blood (live).
What I do is use the CGM reading to determine my glucose trend. Then if I feel I need insulin adjustments, I do a BGM reading to determine how much I need.

author: Dorey King Marcincuk
text: I have this problem too.  (assuming this isn't just a compression error that will self correct)  Once it starts  acting up it gets worse and worse.  Over the 14 days, it starts misleading me into thinking my readings are much better than they are until it eventually starts telling me my readings are consistently  much too low all day and then I know its malfunctioning.  Last time, just to see what it would do, I intentionally ate a slice of pizza followed by a protein bar, both of which should have sent my blood sugar flying.  It did go up, but not nearly enough and went right back to 60 again. Then it cut out before the 14 days.  I don't take any medication, strictly diet.  I use the machine to help me make better diet and exercise decisions, so I know anything low is erroneous.  I checked a few times and it was 30-50 points off.  I'm still trying to figure out what the problem is.  They don't appear to be coming off.  Maybe they get bent?  Maybe I'm getting sensors that are improperly stored?  I'm all ears. The first few I got, which had to be special ordered, worked fine the entire 14 days.
